Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

DeCovarT 2.6.0

Gaussian draws from Cholesky factors

  • simulate_bulk_from_cells(), simulate_bulk_mixture(), simulate_reference_replicates() and the population and single-cell parametric bootstraps draw from the upper Cholesky factor of the covariance (mu + Z R), computed once per cell type, in place of MASS::mvrnorm(). The law is the same; the numbers for a given seed differ from 2.5.0.
  • Cause: MASS::mvrnorm() takes a full eigendecomposition (LAPACK dsyevr). Under OpenBLAS 0.3.20 (Ubuntu 22.04) on an Intel Xeon w9-3575X, dsyevr stopped with “error code 1” on well-conditioned G = 200 covariances of figure 5: 6 failures in 1,004 calls with the SkylakeX kernel, 13 in 502 with Nehalem, 2 with Sandybridge or Prescott, none with Haswell. With the reference LAPACK on the OpenBLAS kernels the same six calls failed; with the reference BLAS none did. The fault is in the OpenBLAS BLAS kernels, not in R, MASS or LAPACK. Draft reports are in scripts/reports/.

Reproducible scenarios

  • run_simulation_benchmark() gains seed (scenario i runs under withr::with_seed(seed + i)) and scenarios (run a subset of rows, keeping their index for the seed). A failed scenario is reproduced exactly with scenarios = i.
  • deconvolute_ratios(label =) logs one line per solver: the scenario label, the solver, the number of bulks, the elapsed time and the fits with no estimate. run_simulation_benchmark(verbose = TRUE) sets it.

DeCovarT 2.5.0

Breaking changes

  • Likelihood objects replace the model string, in the manner of glm(family = binomial). population_likelihood() and single_cell_likelihood() return an object of class decovart_likelihood holding the simulator, log-likelihood, score, Wald standard errors, curvature check, parameter rows and interval menu of each model. deconvolute_ratios() and run_simulation_benchmark() take likelihood = (the object or its constructor) in place of model = "population" | "single_cell".
  • benchmark_likelihood(), exported in 2.4.0, is removed; its functions are fields of the likelihood objects and take (p, y, mu, Sigma).

Boundary estimates

  • L-BFGS-B works on the closed orthant and returns exact zeros: one zero proportion (a face), two (an edge), up to J - 1 (a vertex, one cell type making up the whole sample). Newton-Raphson in ILR coordinates never does. At any such estimate the Wald, ILR and oracle intervals are undefined and are NA, the scale rows of the single-cell model included.
  • The figure 5 crash at G = 200 was a shape error, not a failure of an interval derivation: on a boundary estimate the empty single-cell interval had the J composition rows only, while interior ones also had the four scale rows. Every bulk now has the rows of likelihood$parameters().
  • The optimisation table gains n_zero (zero proportions per bulk) and the interval table n_boundary (bulks with a zero proportion): Wald and ILR coverage is over interior estimates only.
  • The population simulator now draws from generative_mean and generative_sigma when a scenario sets them, as the single-cell one already did; population scenarios do not set them, so their bulks are unchanged.
  • Profile intervals refit from the bulk and do not depend on the solver; the figure scripts now request them under Newton-Raphson only.

DeCovarT 2.4.0

  • Benchmark interval tables tolerate a missing parameter row. When one bulk’s interval omitted a parameter (seen with L-BFGS-B at G = 200 in figure 5), compute_benchmark_metrics() stopped with a subscript error. That bulk now counts as having no interval for the parameter. A sample whose optimiser returns no finite estimate is counted separately in n_numerical_failures, and its convergence record is "numerical failure".

  • Exported for scripts, so none needs ::: or get(). scale_covariances_to_overlap(), hellinger_gaussian() (formerly .hellinger_gaussian()), kkt_residual() (formerly .kkt_residual()) and benchmark_likelihood() (formerly .benchmark_model()).

  • No package-level mutable state. cli and withr move to Imports. The plain-text fallback of the .ui_* wrappers is removed and the package calls cli directly. The single-slot Cholesky cache of the covariance mixture is removed. Estimates are unchanged. Newton fits take 1.1 to 1.4 times as long at G = 20 (about 0.1 s per 200 fits); at G = 200 repeated timings ranged from 0.6 to 1.5 times, because the identity check on the covariance array costs about as much as the factorisation it saves. The qrng-missing note is shown once through cli’s own frequency control; its runif() fallback no longer changes the caller’s random state. .with_seed() delegates to withr::with_seed().

  • New test test-linear-algebra.R fails when BLAS / LAPACK return wrong Cholesky factors or inverses. This happens with OpenBLAS 0.3.20 on Intel Xeon w9-3575X (set OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Haswell before R starts). SkylakeX repairs chol() and solve() but not every dsyevr call; Haswell is the kernel for which both were correct.

  • Simulation benchmarks rebuilt (figures 2, 3 and the new figure 5).

    • deconvolute_ratios_L_BFGS_B() now runs L-BFGS-B on the closure chart p = w / sum(w), w >= 0, and maximises the convolution likelihood itself: box KKT points are simplex KKT points and exact zeros are reachable. The former fit renormalised a box-constrained surrogate, whose faces were not stationary (KKT residual about 0.1). A stick-breaking box was tried first and rejected: once a stick is exhausted the later coordinates have no gradient, and the solver stopped at vertices up to 2.19 log-likelihood units below the maximum (0.0008 at most for the closure chart).
    • deconvolute_single_cell(optimiser = "lbfgsb") maximises the profile log-likelihood on the same chart; bootstrap_decovart() and bootstrap_single_cell() gain optimiser, so bootstrap refits use the optimiser of the estimate.
    • rescale_single_cell_moments(): the cell size now scales the covariance quadratically, S_j^2 Sigma_j^theta, as it scales every gene of a cell; the overlap of two types of equal size no longer depends on that size.
    • scale_covariances_to_overlap(pairs = ) calibrates the mean overlap of selected pairs of types (siblings of a lineage).
    • New simulate_reference_replicates(): an independent reference panel of individuals (and cells) per type, for benchmark methods that estimate the reference moments themselves.
    • run_simulation_benchmark(model = "single_cell", return_data = TRUE, reference = ) simulates bulks from cells, scores the realised fractions and the two scales, and returns the bulks and a reference panel. Each deconvolution entry accepts a ci list; the new intervals table reports, per method and interval construction (Wald, ILR, profile, bootstrap, oracle, and the single-cell REML variants), the coverage with its Wilson Monte Carlo interval, the mean and median width and the share of intervals leaving [0, 1].
    • Figure scripts: scripts/fig02_bivariate_toy.R, scripts/fig03_variance_covariance_driven.R and the new scripts/fig05_single_cell_hierarchical.R (four cell types in two lineages, 32 + 1 scenarios) share one layout: run size from DECOVART_N_REPLICATES, DECOVART_N_BOOT, DECOVART_N_REFERENCE, DECOVART_CORES and DECOVART_POSTPROCESS_ONLY; figXX_benchmark.rds with every result and figXX_plot_data.rds keyed by figure file stem. Figures 3 and 5 add MEAD (R package), RNA-Sieve and ReDeconv (Python, through a uv project in scripts/benchmark_metrics/python/) with gene filters off; DECALS has no public code and is not run.
    • Single-cell intervals and bootstraps also cover the platform scale a = phi / c and the cell count n = c^2 / phi (rows platform_scale_a and cell_count_n), formed on the log scale so both stay positive; the benchmark scores them against the true a and n.
    • generate_random_network_skeleton() accepts block_sizes for a stochastic block model with fixed, contiguous blocks, and returns the block of every gene as attribute "block". Figures 3 and 5 use three blocks of equal size; in figure 5 the two siblings of a lineage share one skeleton (block model for types 1-2, scale-free for types 3-4) and differ only by 5% of sign flips on the lineage’s edge weights.
    • Figures 2, 3 and 5 run NNLS next to lsei; figures 3 and 5 add the robust linear model (deconvolute_ratios_rlm()). RNA-Sieve is scored with its released interval and with the paper’s Fisher and Godambe intervals recomputed on all genes.
    • scripts/auxiliary/ is split into scripts/benchmark_metrics/ and scripts/visualisation/; the vignette figure scripts move to vignettes/scripts/; the bibliography tools in scripts/curate_bibliography/ are a uv project.
    • Theory vignettes are reorganised into population and single-cell references, each split into generative model and optimisation, then inference: theory-population-generative-optimisation, theory-population-inference, theory-single-cell-generative-optimisation and the new theory-single-cell-inference. New vignette fig05-single-cell-hierarchical.

  • Fixes to the interval and test machinery, found by simulation. scripts/benchmark_metrics/check_confidence_interval_coverage.R checks the information matrices against independent computations and the coverage of every interval method (300 replicates).

    • restricted_mle_decovart() and restricted_mle_single_cell() used BFGS from the barycentre; with pooled columns the first step could jump to a vertex, where the likelihood is flat, and stop there (an estimate of (1, 0) for a true (0.7, 0.3)). Both now run the trust-region Newton driver on the face with the pooled analytic Hessian (.fit_on_face()). This affects lrt_decovart(), confint_profile_decovart(), bootstrap_decovart() and the pooled confint_decovart() menu.
    • A profile interval whose upper end reaches the face returned the estimate instead of 1; a failed refit now gives NA with a warning.
    • A null p_j = 1 fixes J - 1 coordinates on faces; the chi-bar-square tests now count them.
    • vcov_single_cell(scales_known = TRUE) gives the covariance of a fixed-scale or two-stage fit instead of the profile covariance.
    • The reference bootstraps regenerate the bulk from the fitted model and refit it with the resampled moments; drawing it from the resampled moments hid the reference error (coverage 0.76 instead of 0.92).
    • Bootstraps report n_failed.
    • confint_single_cell(variance = "reml") and confint_profile_single_cell(variance = "reml") correct for the G - J residual degrees of freedom of the variance scale (covariance inflated by G / (G - J), Student-t quantiles, chi-square interval for phi, exact linear-model profile cut-off). With G = 10 the default "ml" intervals cover 0.84 to 0.93 at the 0.95 level.

  • Smaller, flatter internals. equicorrelation_gram() is no longer exported: generate_mean_signature_matrix(target_cosine = ) builds the same Gram matrix, and its generated means are unchanged bit for bit. The gene frames, the Cholesky test, the two precision-inversion loops, the one-line metrics and the convergence helpers of the benchmark are merged or inlined. Every solver returns one convergence record (code, iterations, message, rdm); compute_benchmark_metrics() loses the unused lower and upper arguments. A seeded gene frame restores the global random state. Simulated covariances are now inverted through the Cholesky factor of the precision (exactly symmetric, three to five times faster than QR, no less accurate); simulated datasets change in their last bits, and through MASS::mvrnorm() in their draws, so benchmarks must be rerun.

  • Confidence intervals for both mixture models. confint_decovart() chooses an interval for the population convolution. The default maps a Wald interval for the ILR coordinate through the inverse chart (confint_ilr_backtransform()). wald is the delta method, firth is a Jeffreys-penalised Wald interval, profile inverts the likelihood ratio, and bootstrap / reference are the existing resamples. confint.decovart_fit() is unchanged and remains the per-column delta method. confint_single_cell() uses the same names for the profile likelihood. Intervals for the composition come from the Schur complement that removes the two scales; intervals for the scales come from the complementary Schur complement, on the log scale by default. deconvolute_single_cell() now returns vcov, vcov_rho and vcov_nuisance. Higher-order and sandwich corrections for a plug-in covariance are not included. With several donors in every cell type the reference bootstrap resamples donors and keeps the bulk fixed; otherwise it resamples columns within each type and regenerates the bulk. Cell-type labels are not shuffled.

  • Single-cell mixture, separate from the population convolution. Cell-level moments and the bulk sum of cells are rescale_single_cell_moments() and simulate_bulk_from_cells(). deconvolute_single_cell() starts from a free-scale non-negative least-squares fit, then profiles the mean and variance scales out in closed form and runs Newton-Raphson on the profile log-likelihood of the ILR coordinates (profile_loglik_single_cell_ilr(), exact score, Schur-complement Hessian). One loop reaches the joint maximum; the former scale/composition alternation needed up to 95 outer updates. profile = FALSE keeps the two-stage plug-in fit for comparison. The fit requires G > J. Default reference: raw cell covariance and cell fractions. The population log-likelihood is unchanged (p^2 covariance weights).

  • Shared ILR chart and Newton driver. The simplex chart (helmert_basis(), isometric_logistic(), repair_simplex(), …) is in R/02_00_ilr_chart.R; the cached covariance factorisation and the nlminb trust-region driver are in R/02_00_likelihood_core.R. Files specific to the p^2 convolution carry a population_ tag (R/01_01_population_toy_simulation.R, R/02_02_population_decovart_estimate_ratios.R, R/02_03_population_decovart_fit.R). The Newton driver now sets abs.tol = 0: PORT’s absolute-function test assumes a nonnegative objective, and a negative log-likelihood can cross zero.

  • Benchmark code split into run, metrics and visualisation. R/04_01_run_benchmark.R fits every algorithm to every sample; R/04_02_run_simulation_benchmark.R runs the scenario grid; R/04_03_performance_metrics_global.R scores the whole composition vector; R/04_04_performance_metrics_celltype.R scores each cellular ratio across replicates (Pearson, presence F1, bias, coverage). Plots move to R/05_01_monte_carlo_plots.R and R/05_02_algorithm_similarity.R, with a third call graph. Entropy, MixSim overlap, Jeffreys divergence and the () parser move to the scenario files (01_03, 01_04); repair_simplex() to the estimation file.

  • Removed from the package. plot_correlation_Heatmap() (its input columns no longer exist in benchmark output), check_true_theta() (a wrapper of the internal parser), spd_affine_invariant_distance() (folded into compute_average_riemannian()), compute_glmnet_gene_scores() (moved, with its cross-validated variant, to scripts/experimental/compute_glmnet_gene_scores.R), and the unexported file writers. Scores that do not apply in a benchmark table are now NA instead of the string "irrelevant". The package no longer writes files (srr G4.0 is now not applicable).

  • Script helpers out of R/. write_simulation_artefacts(), read_simulation_artefacts(), the fig02 / fig03 factor orders and display labels, and the expected-Fisher Wald refresh move to scripts/auxiliary/benchmark_artefacts.R. The figure-book scripts become scripts/visualisation/05_03 to 05_06, loaded together by scripts/visualisation/load_visualisation.R. The fig02, fig03 and regen scripts now source that loader: before, they called the book functions without sourcing the files that define them.

  • Bug fix: Hessian for four or more cell types. hessian_loglik_unconstrained() filled its lower triangle with H[lower.tri(H)] <- H[upper.tri(H)], which pairs the wrong entries as soon as (J): the returned matrix was neither symmetric nor the Hessian. Newton–Raphson (the fit_decovart() default), Marquardt–Levenberg, hessian_loglik_constrained() and the eigenvalues of boundary_diagnostics() were affected for (J); the score and the Fisher (Wald) covariance were not. The score, Hessian and expected Fisher information are now vectorised around one shared information block (about six times faster), and a (J=4) test checks the Hessian against numDeriv.

  • Dense covariance only; structured backends move to scripts/experimental/. new_decovart_covariance(), sigma_logdet(), sigma_solve(), sigma_quadform(), sigma_trace_precision_times() and covariance_structure_from_graph_model() leave the package, and .sigma_p_factorisation() loses its backend argument. The appendix S2 script sources scripts/experimental/covariance_backends.R. Matrix is no longer imported.

  • Fixed-covariance GLS competitor removed. fixed_gls_covariance() and deconvolute_ratios_gls() leave the package; the S4 script and the S1 vignette compute the mean-only GLS fit locally.

  • Inference split by geometry. R/03_01_interior_intervals.R (Wald and profile-likelihood intervals), R/03_02_boundary_tests.R (restricted MLE on faces, chi-bar-square, likelihood-ratio tests, boundary diagnostics) and R/03_03_resampling_inference.R (parametric and reference bootstraps, equivariance check). multistart_decovart() moves next to starting_simplex().

  • Simpler inference interface. restricted_mle_decovart() is now the single fitting engine: y may be a vector or a (GN) matrix of replicates, and fixed = NULL gives the unrestricted MLE on the closed simplex. The bulk_expression argument of lrt_decovart(), confint_profile_decovart(), bootstrap_decovart(), equivariance_check_decovart() and reference_bootstrap_decovart() is removed: pass replicates as the columns of y. Constrained ratios must be named by cell types (integer indices are no longer accepted). reference_bootstrap_decovart() takes a named list of purified matrices only (cell_type_labels removed). profile_loglik_decovart() and the internal .inner_product() are removed.

  • File layout and dropped ALR helpers. Source files now follow the article: 01_ simulations, 02_ optimisation and estimation, 03_ intervals, 04_ benchmarks. additive_logistic(), additive_log_ratio() and their Jacobian and Hessian leave the package; solvers use the isometric log-ratio chart. Figure scripts that still draw an ALR surface keep those two maps under scripts/auxiliary/.

  • Confidence intervals: regularity, geometry and the three tests. The MLE vignette and the article appendix now state the regularity conditions of the large-sample approximation (interior truth, fixed dimension, replication over biological samples, not genes), add the small-dispersion limit in the number of cells for one bulk sample, compare Wald, likelihood-ratio and score tests and their inversion into intervals, treat nuisance scales through the envelope theorem and parameter orthogonality, and describe higher-order corrections (modified likelihood root, Bartlett). The logit-scale Wald route and the variational sandwich are removed. The article now splits each model into optimisation and inference, moves the chart choice, the single-cell fit and the robust variants to the appendix, derives Fisher scoring as iteratively reweighted least squares, and groups the perspectives into modelling, optimisation and estimating-equation inference (GEE, GMM, HC corrections).

  • reference_bootstrap_decovart() loses method = "dirichlet". The Dirichlet composition sweep measured performance across random mixtures, not uncertainty for one observed bulk, so it is removed together with its dirichlet_alpha argument and p_simulated output. The function now always needs y or bulk_expression and resamples donors (default) or cells within each cell type, with replacement. Random Dirichlet starting points of the solvers are unchanged.

  • Fig02 performance books. Twelve meta-scenario pages (small then large CLD; homoscedastic then heteroscedastic; balanced / moderately / highly unbalanced), each a 2-by-2 of correlation corners ((0,0)), ((-0.8,-0.8)), ((0.8,0.8)), ((-0.8,0.8)). Similarity heatmaps cluster paired (p) within each corner and draw a dendrogram on the right, flush with the tiles. Wald forests omit NNLS, LSEI, and SA. Whiskers use the expected-Fisher SE at the true composition (confint.decovart_fit / vcov_ilr_delta; constant per scenario) together with the empirical Monte Carlo SD; bold two-line geom_label boxes (one per solver, vertically centred between the two cell types) report RMSE and coverage, which coincide for (p_1) and (p_2) on the unit simplex. Rainclouds plot (p) with vertical lines at the true proportions on a 30-inch canvas and translucent slabs. A 12-page solver-dot book uses the same 9-by-9 correlation factorial as the RMSE heatmaps (enrichplot-style: colour RMSE, size Aitchison; horizontal y-axis labels). ggplot data for each book (not rgl) is written to output/fig02/ggplot_rds/. Scenario factors are relevelled with forcats (Suggests) when artefacts are read.

  • Fig02 density books. Kernel-density rasters fill the gene-axis window (no inner white frame). Bulk pages drop the 95% Gaussian ellipses with a (^2_2) footnote. ILR profiles use () so unbalanced compositions are not cropped, and plot the relative likelihood L/\max L on a log10 y-axis with annotation_logticks(). Page titles follow the same CLD / variance / composition order as the performance books. Log-likelihood outputs split into loglik_surface_p.pdf (ratio lattice), loglik_ilr_profile.pdf (ILR () profile with MLE), and loglik_rgl.pdf plus interactive loglik_rgl.html.

  • Fig03 covariance-driven grid. G=20, J=3. Graph generators are scale-free and cluster (stochastic block model) only: a 2^{2} assignment on the mean-collinear types, type 3 held at scale-free, times three target MixSim average overlaps (global covariance scale, precision zeros kept; 4\times 3\times 3=36 scenarios). hybrid_config.rds stores graph_generators (model + graph_params per cell type) alongside true_theta, plus realised BarOmega, f_{\mathrm{cov}}, and pairwise AIRM distance. Convolution-likelihood solvers attach interior simplex standard errors from vcov_ilr_delta() inside deconvolute_ratios() (the same object as vcov.decovart_fit() / confint.decovart_fit()). Mean-only solvers (NNLS, LSEI) leave coverage, mean model SE, and se_sd_ratio missing. The ALR helper vcov_alr_delta() has been removed.

  • Fig03 latent-space and resource books. save_hybrid_latent_projection_book() writes a 16-page 2-D book (extreme MixSim overlap () extreme Shannon composition () four CT1/CT2 topologies). The top row is independent Thomson factanal() scores per type; the bottom row is a shared MCFA plane on convolution draws, MCFA on an unsupervised mixture with weights (), and supervised MclustDR. Runtime and memory rainclouds (save_hybrid_runtime_book(), save_hybrid_memory_book()) use one page per composition, facet overlap, and log10 y with a rug of Monte Carlo draws. Fig02 has the matching pair save_bivariate_runtime_book() / save_bivariate_memory_book() (correlation corners on the x-axis).

  • Overlap in moderate dimension. compute_average_overlap() uses MixSim Davies quadrature for G<4 and stratified Sobol Monte Carlo (overlap_gaussian_mc(), default 10^4 draws per component) when G\ge 4. scale_covariances_to_overlap() calibrates a global covariance scale to a target average overlap. Affine-invariant Riemannian distance of the \Sigma_j is riemannian_sigma. Theory: vignettes/theory-distance-covariance.qmd.

  • Faceted plots. theme_decovart_facets() (black strips, panel border, after the atlas-feature-selection-benchmark theme_features) is the default for forest, raincloud, metric tiles, and similarity heatmaps. Fig02 PDFs are written under output/fig02/density_visualisations/ and output/fig02/performance_visualisations/ at a wide canvas and 320 dpi.

  • Simulation artefacts. write_simulation_artefacts() / read_simulation_artefacts() persist the design grid, scenario descriptors (including Jeffreys), \theta, and ADEMP metrics as four RDS files keyed by ID. The written config uses the canonical design columns (proportions, centroids) and drops true_theta (stored in the theta artefact) and scenario_idx (encoded in ID). Fig02 IDs are B{idx}_{Ho|He}_{Ba|Mo|Hi}_{Sm|Lg}.

  • Scenario descriptors. describe_simulation_scenario() now reports max_cosine, mean_euclidean (centroid / CLD gap), unweighted pairwise Hellinger (hellinger; the distance is symmetric) plus optional hellinger_weighted, and keeps Jeffreys as a supplementary column on the descriptors artefact.

  • Bivariate figures. Purified and bulk 2-D densities fill the gene-axis window with a MASS::kde2d() raster (viridis). Purified pages keep red-circle / green-triangle centroids and exact 95% Gaussian ellipses (gaussian_confidence_ellipse()); bulk pages keep centroids only. Bulk pages collect a shared legend with cowplot::get_legend(). Log-likelihood books evaluate ((p_1,p_2)) on a ratio lattice (not gene space): ggplot rasters versus a true rgl::persp3d() surface that marks the simulation proportions. plot_mc_raincloud(include_dots = FALSE, max_rows = …) avoids the quadprog long-vector crash on the 972-scenario grid.

  • Negative bulk. .prepare_deconvolution_inputs() warns on negative expression instead of aborting. run_simulation_benchmark() no longer floors Gaussian draws at 0.

  • Scenario 3 (variance-driven). Fixed Gram \cos(\mu_1,\mu_2)=0.9, \cos(\mu_j,\mu_3)=0.1; 2^3 graph assignments (Erdős–Rényi / scale-free) \times three precision cushions; compositions from composition_from_entropy() at H^{\star}\in\{1,0.5,0.1\}; solvers LSEI, CIBERSORT, L-BFGS-B, Newton–Raphson, Marquardt–Levenberg (n=50, G=10). Descriptor docs use one callout per family in the synthetic-scenarios vignette. kappa_sigma_p is now returned beside the reciprocal ratio. generate_mean_signature_matrix(nonnegative = TRUE) uses a disjoint-support frame so signatures stay nonnegative. Graph precisions are completed by a uniform spectral shift and extra-loaded until both \Omega and \Sigma=\Omega^{-1} admit a Cholesky factor (support and signs of W unchanged). Failed \hat p entries are treated as absent when scoring presence F1. simulate_bulk_mixture(truncate_negative = TRUE) floors bulk coordinates at 0 (used by run_simulation_benchmark()).

  • Terminal UI. Optional Suggests cli formats messages, warnings and errors (cli_alert_* / cli_abort, with base message() / stop() fallback). run_simulation_benchmark(verbose = TRUE) logs each scenario row; grids of 10 or fewer scenarios also tick every 10 inferred samples.

  • Documentation layout. Paper scenarios live in the fig02-bivariate-toy and fig03-variance-driven articles (one script each: scripts/fig02_bivariate_toy.R, scripts/fig03_variance_driven.R). Regular-case MLE checks and identifiability sit in Appendix S1. ADEMP / Nature Methods reporting is at the end of vignettes/theory-synthetic-scenarios-mean-covariance.qmd.

  • Monte Carlo figures. pivot_mc_estimates(), plot_mc_raincloud() (ggplot2 + ggdist horizontal rainclouds of \hat p_j-p_j^{\star}), plot_mc_forest() (ADEMP summaries with Wilson whiskers on the coverage rate), plot_algorithm_similarity() (geom_tile + hclust(1-r)), and plot_mc_metric_dots() (faceted min-max scores; no default composite). Optional Suggests: ggdist, ggdendro. ComplexHeatmap remains for linked multi-omics grids only.

  • Solver starts. starting_simplex() (used by all ILR maps) accepts the barycentre (default), a Dirichlet draw (initial_p = "dirichlet", dirichlet_alpha = 1 uniform on the simplex; \alpha>1 centre-biased; \alpha<1 face-biased; several independent draws for multistarts), or a mean-only simplex QP (initial_p = "qp" via deconvolute_ratios_deconrnaseq()). multistart_decovart() uses the Dirichlet path.

  • Fixed-covariance GLS competitor. deconvolute_ratios_gls() wraps MASS::lm.gls() with a known G\times G residual covariance; fixed_gls_covariance() builds the global-diagonal W at a declared p (default 1/J). Unconstrained OLS (deconvolute_ratios_lsfit) has been removed.

  • ILR / Helmert simplex chart. Frequentist solvers and vcov.decovart_fit() now use isometric log-ratio coordinates on a Helmert basis (helmert_basis(), isometric_logistic(), isometric_log_ratio(), jacobian_isometric_logistic(), hessian_isometric_logistic(), vcov_ilr_delta()). No cell type is pinned as a reference; changing the ILR basis by an orthogonal rotation leaves (), (()) and (()) unchanged. Additive log-ratio maps remain exported for the derivatives vignette appendix. Restricted MLE assembly treats a fully constrained face without calling ILR on an empty coordinate, and an unrestricted fit that sits near a face is compared with the exact-face restricted MLE so the reported point can be the closed-simplex supremum.

  • Gram-matrix mean signatures. generate_mean_signature_matrix() realises a target cosine Gram via the symmetric square root (=s,QR^{1/2}) (equicorrelation_gram() or target_gram). Pairwise cosines match (R) exactly; the previous shared-plus-private blend is documented as an appendix construction that does not hit () at finite (J).

  • Identifiability. Full column rank of () is sufficient but not necessary: identical means remain identifiable when the cell-type covariances differ. The article and MLE vignette now state injectivity of (p(p,(p))).

  • Benchmark metrics and sample-level parallelism. compute_benchmark_metrics() now returns a three-block list: composition / regression scores (global TV, RMSE, angular distance, SDID, MaxAE; cell-type Pearson, presence F1, and false-positive mass), ADEMP Monte Carlo summaries, and optimisation / runtime diagnostics (simplex KKT residual, numerical versus theoretical convergence, per-sample elapsed time, and ps PSS memory). Coverage of the Monte Carlo coverage rate uses a Wilson interval by default (coverage_mc_interval(); Wald and Agresti–Coull optional). run_simulation_benchmark() also returns theta_true (the convolution parameters), descriptors / supplementary from describe_simulation_scenario(), and call (match.call()). MixSim BarOmega and averaged pairwise Hellinger are kept in descriptors; Jeffreys overlap is supplementary. deconvolute_ratios() iterates bulk columns with furrr when cores > 1, using L’Ecuyer-CMRG streams (furrr_options(seed = TRUE)). Scenario rows are sequential, so workers are never nested. There is no composite global score.

  • Structure-aware covariance backends. New new_decovart_covariance() wraps with a declared structure ("dense", "block", "band", "sparse", "diag_lowrank") and exposes operators sigma_logdet(), sigma_solve(), sigma_quadform() and sigma_trace_precision_times() that return the log-determinant and solves without materialising a dense precision. Block Cholesky (disconnected modules / stochastic block model), banded Cholesky (band / AR), sparse Cholesky with a cached symbolic ordering (Erdős–Rényi, scale-free, small-world), and the Woodbury / matrix-determinant-lemma path for diagonal-plus-low-rank covariances (shared regulatory programs; Sigma = W W^T + Psi) each match the dense default to machine precision. covariance_structure_from_graph_model() maps a network topology to the recommended backend, and .sigma_p_factorisation() gains an optional backend argument. Band and sparse backends use the imported Matrix package. See the new “Structure-aware covariance backends” section of vignette("theory-decovart-generative-model") and scripts/supp_S2_covariance_inversion.R.

DeCovarT 2.3.1

  • CRAN resubmission. Tests no longer write under the package tree. The bivariate toy scenario is built in memory by new_bivariate_toy_scenario() in tests/testthat/helper.R; the former fixtures/make-useful-things.R writer and its golden RDS files are gone. CRAN Quarto vignettes do not execute library(DeCovarT) during rebuild (Windows CLI subprocess cannot see R CMD build’s temporary library).

DeCovarT 2.3.0

  • Log-likelihood evaluation. loglik_multivariate() now uses the cached Cholesky factor with backsolve() for the Mahalanobis term, matching mvtnorm::dmvnorm(..., log = TRUE) up to ((2)), rather than a dense ({}{-1}). The inverse remains cached for the analytic score and Hessian.

  • Corrected log-likelihood (breaking numerical change). loglik_multivariate() implemented instead of the Gaussian , doubling the determinant contribution. The objective now matches mvtnorm::dmvnorm(..., log = TRUE) up to , and holds exactly, so the objective and the Wald / Fisher inference are finally consistent. gradient_loglik_unconstrained() and hessian_loglik_unconstrained() halve their determinant terms accordingly; residual terms and expected_fisher_unconstrained() are unchanged. Reported log-likelihood values, AIC and likelihood-ratio statistics all change; point estimates move only slightly. The article and the derivatives vignette were updated in step.

  • Likelihood-ratio and boundary inference. New lrt_decovart(), confint_profile_decovart(), profile_loglik_decovart(), restricted_mle_decovart(), chi_bar_square_pvalue() and bootstrap_decovart(). Testing the absence of a cell type puts the null on a simplex face, where Wilks’ theorem fails and ALR Wald intervals are undefined; the null law is the chi-bar-square mixture of Chernoff (1954) and Self and Liang (1987), with a restricted parametric bootstrap when the binomial weights cannot be justified. Profile intervals are reparametrisation-invariant and stay inside . reference_bootstrap_decovart() resamples the experimental units of a labelled reference: donors within each cell type (default), cells within each cell type, or Dirichlet draws of the composition. Gene-order and cell-type-label shuffles of an averaged signature are not inferential procedures; equivariance_check_decovart() only verifies that permuting signature columns relabels .

  • Boundary and multimodality diagnostics. New boundary_diagnostics() and multistart_decovart(), wired into fit_decovart(n_starts =, boundary_tol =) and stored in fit$diagnostics. The realised log-likelihood is not globally concave (a worked indefinite-Hessian counterexample is in the new vignette), so converged, local_maximum, near_boundary and multimodal are reported as separate claims. A near-boundary estimate is flagged as a caution about Wald linearisation, not as optimiser failure.

  • Numerical stability of additive_logistic(). Now evaluated through the log-sum-exp shift instead of exp(rho) / sum(exp(rho)), which overflowed to NaN for and could make non-factorisable when the MLE approached a simplex face.

  • New vignette vignette("DeCovarT-MLE-properties"): identifiability, existence, failure of uniqueness for one observed sample, population consistency through the Kullback–Leibler divergence and the Fisher information metric, affine (but not logarithmic) equivariance, the four strata of the simplex and their tangent cones, and why replication is what makes the asymptotics meaningful.

DeCovarT 2.2.3

  • Optional heatmap stack. Moved ComplexHeatmap, circlize, and viridis from Imports to Suggests. plot_correlation_Heatmap() guards with requireNamespace() and a clear install message. Removed Additional_repositories (Bioconductor is a standard CRAN dependency source; that field was causing the availability ? ? NOTE).

DeCovarT 2.2.2

  • CRAN resubmission. Quarto Markdown tables in the two CRAN vignettes (no tinytable during vignette rebuild on Windows); absolute pkgdown URLs for articles excluded from the tarball; Rd figure widths in pixels; cran-comments clarifies DESCRIPTION Hunspell false positives.

DeCovarT 2.2.0

  • Model-fit wrapper. Added fit_decovart(), an S3 wrapper in the style of standard R model fits (print, summary, coef, fitted, residuals, vcov, nobs, confint, plot). This makes DeCovarT more versatile and easier for the R statistical community to adopt. deconvolute_ratios() remains the multi-algorithm benchmark tibble. There is no formula / predict() method: the estimator is a variance model, not OLS for bulk expression.

  • fit_decovart() solvers. Marquardt–Levenberg, L-BFGS-B and Newton–Raphson only; ALR maps already land on the simplex (no repair_simplex() on these three).

  • Gene-wise standardise. Affine z-score of bulk, means and covariances (equivariant MLE). Log2 mixing (scaled = TRUE) is rejected (Jensen / CIBERSORT linear space).

  • Wald vcov. Expected Fisher information of the multivariate normal convolution, mapped to the simplex by the ALR delta method.

  • Methods paper on the site. pkgdown embeds article/main.pdf via the embedpdf Quarto extension (vignette DeCovarT methods paper).

DeCovarT 2.0.0

  • Release aligned with the GitHub v2.0.0 tag and the first CRAN submission, focused on numerical stability and optimiser cost in R/03_03_DeCovarT_estimate_ratios_frequentist.R (documented in vignette("generative-model-derivatives"), section Numerical speed-ups and solver safeguards). The CRAN tarball ships the use-cases and softmax/ALR vignettes; remaining articles stay on the pkgdown site.

  • Newton–Raphson evaluation budget. Removed an erroneous eval.max = 1 control passed to stats::nlminb() in deconvolute_ratios_Newton_Raphson(), which capped the entire run at a single objective evaluation and silently returned the equi-balanced start.

  • Cached Cholesky factorisation of \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p}). New internal .sigma_p_factorisation() assembles the mixture covariance once per trial point, shares chol() / chol2inv() across the log-likelihood, gradient and Hessian, and uses a Cholesky-based log-determinant (verified against numDeriv).

  • Analytic gradient for L-BFGS-B. deconvolute_ratios_L_BFGS_B() now passes the unconstrained analytic score instead of finite differences, with finite-penalty guards when box-constrained line searches drive \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p}) near-singular.

  • marqLevAlg Hessian sign under maximisation. When minimize = FALSE, marqLevAlg only negates fn / gr; the analytic Hessian must be negated by hand so the Commenges et al. RDM criterion can fire. Reported upstream as VivianePhilipps/marqLevAlgParallel#3.

  • Documentation. Expanded use-cases and feature-selection vignettes; CRAN-oriented DESCRIPTION (MIT licence, arXiv method reference doi:10.48550/arXiv.2309.09557).

DeCovarT 1.0.0

  • First stabilised release of DeCovarT (semver 1.0.0), marking the end of the exploratory 0.x series. The core ALR-based frequentist deconvolution API, analytic score equations, and simulation tooling are now treated as a stable public surface for downstream use and paper reproduction.

  • Analytic derivatives, numerically verified. The unconstrained and constrained log-likelihood gradients and Hessians (and the additive logistic Jacobian / Hessian) are derived in closed form and unit-tested against numDeriv finite differences. Earlier faulty numerical / finite-difference-only paths that could mislead Marquardt–Levenberg and related optimisers have been replaced by these verified analytic expressions (see vignette("generative-model-derivatives") and tests/testthat/test-03_03_DeCovarT.R).

  • Simulation framework beyond the bivariate toy. Synthetic first- and second-order moments now support arbitrary gene panels (G\gg 2) and multi-type mixtures: AutoGeneS-style mean signatures with a cosine dial, graph-constrained precisions (ER, hub/star, scale-free, SBM, small-world), and bulk convolution via simulate_bulk_mixture(). A hybrid multi-topology reference scenario (G=50, J=3) in scripts/generate_random_markov_network.R and vignette("synthetic-scenarios") stresses feature selection under EE / DE / differential-modality-like blocks (scDD / muscat-inspired taxonomy).

  • Feature-selection metrics (compute_average_overlap(), compute_average_jeffreys(), compute_glmnet_gene_scores()) and a shared check_true_theta() validator complete the end-to-end simulation → pre-screen → NSGA-II refinement loop documented in vignette("feature-selection").

DeCovarT 0.1.0

  • First official release of DeCovarT: bulk transcriptomic deconvolution that accounts for gene-gene covariance in purified reference populations.
